forecaster_note: Clean head-high-plus for the S-exposed breaks in the AM, smaller but still clean elsewhere. Then winds go light to moderate S/SE for bumpy but doable surf in the afternoon — S corners stay clean but small. Looking ahead, Monday is the one to circle: a pulse of long-period S swell arrives, bigger than the spot forecasts show, with powerful overhead surf at the south-exposed breaks and favourable AM offshores. — Surfline Sydney Regional Forecast

wind.summary: WSW 7 km/h at dawn — light, clean offshore holding through to about 11am. Swings SE from midday and builds to 12 km/h onshore by 3pm, gusting 15 at dusk. The clean window is 6:19–11am.

shark.summary: SharkSmart NSW live: no shark detections or drone sightings at any of your four spots in the last 24 h. Most recent Northern Beaches sightings were Palm Beach (3:55pm) and Mona Vale (11:03am) on 27 Aug — both ~48 h ago and well north of Dee Why. Feed is healthy: latest statewide tagged detection 6:59am today, 18 in the last 24 h.

days.label: Today
days.note: Your window is the morning and it is a good one. Energy climbs from 512 kJ at dawn to a peak 601 kJ at 9am with 100/100 consistency, and the WSW offshore holds until about 11am — Surfline has Dee Why at Fair–Good in exactly that block. Direction is the catch again: 5.9ft @ 10s from 157° is SSE, which is why Long Reef is 5–7ft and Manly only 3–4ft. High tide 8:48am, so the 9–11am push is the sweet spot. SE onshore kills it from midday.

swells.label: Small E swell (fills in from midday)

dee-why.window: 9–11am is the pick — Fair–Good on Surfline, 601 kJ, offshore WSW and the last of the push to the 8:48am high. Dawn works too at 3–4ft+ but it is a size band smaller and 90 kJ softer.
alerts: SE wind arrives around midday and turns it Fair/bumpy by 3pm
Primary at 157° is southerly enough that the open beach will be shifty — the Point carries this one

tip.label: Frontside at the Point, 9am not 6am
tip.text: Unlike a dead-S 180° day, 157° has a touch more east in it, so it bends into the Point better and still lets the bay work on the bigger sets. 601 kJ at 9am with 100/100 consistency means the sets keep arriving — no need to scrap for the first thing that moves. Go frontside on the Point rights, use the tide push to 8:48am, and be out before the SE fills in. That 2.2ft @ 9s from 88° sits inside your 30–80° sweet spot but is too small to shape the session today.

long-reef.window: 6:19–10am if you want the size. Offshore early, but it is a committed paddle and the SE ruins it after midday.
alerts: Biggest of the four — 5–7ft at 9am, building toward 6–8ft by midday as the swell peaks
Grows through the morning while the wind deteriorates — the two curves cross around 11am

tip.label: The most wave, the shortest fuse
tip.text: The reef faces straight into 157°, so it converts the whole 5.9ft @ 10s and stacks it. Well overhead with 601 kJ behind it is a proper session and inside your range as a strong paddler, but it is a step-up board and a full commitment, not a casual sample. Curious detail: it keeps building to 6–8ft by noon just as the SE arrives, so the biggest surf of the day will also be the messiest. Go at 6:30am or not at all.

curl-curl.window: 6:30–11am. North Curly corner for the cleanest shape and some shelter from the sweep.
alerts: Sweep will be running with 5.9ft of SSE swell on the banks
Drops to bumpy Fair once the SE fills in after midday

tip.label: The sensible middle ground
tip.text: Curly is the classic S-swell magnet, so it converts more than Dee Why without reaching Long Reef's size — 4–6ft is right in the band you actually enjoy. North Curly corner holds the best shape and cuts the sweep. With 601 kJ pushing water down the beach, pick one bank and keep re-lining off a fixed marker rather than drifting.

manly.window: Any time before midday — it is the most forgiving of the four but also the smallest.
alerts: Smallest of the four — the headland blocks most of the 157° swell

tip.label: Only if you want an easy one
tip.text: North Steyne sits in the shadow of the headland for SSE swell, so all that 601 kJ arrives as waist-to-chest. Clean and rippable, but on a morning where Dee Why is Fair–Good at chest-to-head with the same offshore, there is no reason to drive past it. Keep Manly in the back pocket for when the swell swings NE.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: A big step down in power — energy collapses from 190 kJ at dawn to 116 kJ by 9am, roughly a fifth of today's peak. The upside is a cleaner, longer offshore: WNW 7–8 km/h holds past 11am before the SE returns. Long Reef is the standout at Fair–Good, and the first 16s long-period S lines start showing on the buoys — the front edge of Monday's pulse.

dee-why.window: 6:20–9am while there is still 190 kJ in it. After 9am it drops to 116 kJ and goes soft.
alerts: Sharp energy drop-off through the morning — dawn is materially better than mid-morning

long-reef.window: 6:20–10am — the only Fair–Good rating on the board tomorrow, and by far the best size-to-cleanliness trade.
alerts: Holds 4–5ft while everywhere else halves — the reef is doing the work

curl-curl.window: 6:30–11am. Holds size better than Dee Why but the punch is gone.

manly.window: Morning only — Surfline drops it to Poor–Fair by mid-afternoon.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: You are already in it, and today is the better half by a clear margin — 601 kJ versus 190 kJ, and Dee Why is the only Fair–Good beachie of the two days. If you only get one paddle, make it this morning at the Point. Tomorrow's consolation is Long Reef at Fair–Good, 4–5ft and clean. The real story sits just past the weekend: Monday brings a long-period S pulse the spot forecasts are understating, powerful overhead surf at the S-exposed breaks with AM offshores. Worth keeping Monday morning free.

dee-why.window: Saturday 9–11am is the weekend's best session at Dee Why. Sunday is a dawn-only consolation.
alerts: Both days go onshore SE from midday — mornings only

long-reef.window: Most consistent of the four across both days — 5–7ft Saturday, 4–5ft and Fair–Good Sunday.
alerts: Saturday's size demands a step-up board and a committed session

curl-curl.window: North Curly corner both mornings — the reliable middle option.
alerts: Sweep on Saturday with the bigger SSE swell

manly.window: Smallest option all weekend — the headland blocks the SSE angle both days.
